correctness.rationale: For every cubic edge the count condition is exactly s(u)+s(v)=2x_e. Exhaustive endpoint signed-degree pairs partition into two nonadjacent vertex classes; connectedness makes one global. The monochromatic degree-3 vertices are an efficient dominating set, and the converse construction checks the same equation on both possible edge types. Both recovery directions are unique, and closed-neighbourhood counting yields both modular obstructions. The independent finite script verified the setwise bijection on 19 cubic graphs; this is supplemental to the proof.

originality.rationale: Compared the new unrestricted cubic correspondence (including exact 2p(G) count and bipartite 8-divisibility) against the full pertinent text of three recent foundational strong-majority edge-colouring papers and a published exact result for complete graphs. The latter treats K4, just one cubic graph, and general many-colour sufficient conditions do not imply the two-colour converse or the counting bijection. Efficient domination is classical, but the correspondence to the newly introduced strong-majority edge-colouring problem was not found in those sources. Remaining priority uncertainty is stated explicitly.
residual_risks: A separately indexed or older statement of the same equivalence under perfect-code or majority-colouring terminology may exist.
Classification of efficient codes in restricted cubic families is extensive; such results are not claimed novel and may provide preexisting corollaries.

value.rationale: Establishes a complete structural and enumerative characterization of a new edge-colouring invariant on all connected cubic graphs through a classical perfect-code object; supplies an exact 2p(G) labelled count, decision equivalence, and necessary 4- and bipartite 8-divisibility obstructions. The all-colouring bijection and sharp structural necessity go beyond small examples or textbook parity checks.
